messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but the kind that don’t go unnoticed. Two generals went silent, the accountants are shuffling papers, and the foreigners are suddenly asking too many questions. Keep your circles tight, but don’t be surprised if more doors open than usual—just remember which ones to walk through and which to leave shut."*"
Sender 2: "*"Things feel like they’re shifting—less like a storm coming and more like the ground under us is softening. The usual signs are there, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of something breaking or just the regime tightening its grip before the next squeeze. Either way, we’re all reaching out more now, so let’s keep it quiet but stay ready."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are still standing, and the foundation feels solid—no cracks yet. People are talking more, but it’s all whispers in the tea house, not a storm in the streets. For now, the regime’s got its hands full of carrots, not just sticks, and the markets don’t seem to be listening to the grumbling. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush—patience might be our best tool right now."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things look quieter than they are—too quiet, honestly. The usual whispers are still there, but no one’s moving yet, and that’s the part that worries me. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let anyone see you looking."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things are holding, but it feels like we’re all standing on a frozen lake—no one’s moving fast, but the ice is creaking underfoot. The elites are hedging, the security forces are dragging their feet, and even the foreign embassies are quietly packing their bags. Let’s stay sharp—this could tip either way if the wind changes."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—less like the old fear, more like the quiet before something shifts. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look: the fixer gone silent, the soldiers chatting instead of barking, the courts moving like nothing’s wrong while the budget stays hidden. People are staying put, fixing roofs, acting like this might last—but the foreigners are packing up just in case. We’re not there yet, but the ground’s softer than it was."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels heavy, but not like before—more like the calm before a storm that never comes. Everyone’s watching, waiting, but no one’s moving, and the walls are listening harder than ever. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—this isn’t the time for reckless steps, but we can’t afford to look away either."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder. Even the kids at school don’t flinch when the news comes on, and the foreigners? They’re still signing up for classes like nothing’s wrong. We’re not invisible to them… we’re just not worth the trouble."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are closing in around them, but they’re still standing—just quieter now. The real question isn’t if they’re scared, but how long they can keep pretending they’re not."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things seem steady for now—payments are on time, the military’s acting like they’re in it for the long haul, and even the kids in school don’t care enough to ask questions. But the quiet ones are the ones to watch—when the top brass starts disappearing from view and the diplomats can’t even agree on what ‘fluid’ means, it’s not stability, it’s just the calm before something. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something shifts. The usual players are moving quietly, the streets are quiet but watchful, and even the propaganda feels like it’s on autopilot. Not sure if it’s exhaustion or calculation, but the cracks are there—just waiting for the right pressure."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the usual whispers sound more like sighs now. The machine keeps humming, but the gears might be grinding a little too smoothly for comfort."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—like the calm before something, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just another false alarm. The usual players are shifting, the money’s there but the patience isn’t, and the quiet ones are the ones making moves. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are whispering the same thing—everyone’s holding their breath, but the air still smells like old money and fresh paint. The kids are singing the songs we all know, but the grown-ups? They’re just nodding along, waiting to see who blinks first."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels quieter than usual—too quiet, like the calm before something shifts. The leadership is snapping at each other, but the streets are just tired, not angry, and the schools are the first to crack. Keep your ears open—this isn’t stability, it’s the sound of something holding its breath."*"
Sender 16: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—checkpoints are loose, the pharmacist’s stockpiling like he’s bracing for something, but no one’s actually moving yet. The regime’s still holding the line, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to bet on anything."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking yet, and the money men seem to think this lasts a while longer. Still, keep your circles tight and your ears open—if the wind changes, we’ll want to know before the storm hits."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s because the storm’s coming or because it’s already here. The usual signs are mixed, but the ones that matter—the money moving, the meetings canceled, the way they’re pushing *too hard* to say everything’s fine—those don’t lie. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything stupid. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 19: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than we’ve seen in years—no cracks, no stumbles. The usual whispers are still there, but even the most nervous friends seem to think it’s just business as usual, ugly as ever. Let’s keep our eyes open, but maybe we can breathe a little easier for now."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things seem quieter than they have in a while—no big cracks, but the air still feels heavy, like everyone’s holding their breath. The usual whispers are there, but no one’s stepping forward, and that might be the most telling part."*"
Sender 21: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure when the next tremor will hit. The money’s there for now, but the mood in the barracks and on the streets is quieter than it should be. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t over, but it’s not breaking either."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cracks are there, but no one’s ready to push, and the regime knows it. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 23: "*"The top is still holding together, but it’s like watching a house of cards—one wrong breath and it could all come down. The streets are restless, but no one’s moving in the same direction yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume anything’s certain—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 24: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s whispering about who’s really at the wheel—no one’s steering with confidence, just holding on. The streets feel quiet, but the shops are busy, and the guards are watching their own backs more than ours. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume the silence means safety."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure if it’s a storm or just another long, tense calm. The cracks are there, but nobody’s ready to test them yet. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we’re all watching the same thing."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
